sample_unit: clinicians receiving at least one ECG-ML alert (1385 ECG-ML-positive patients)
models_evaluated: ECG-based machine learning (ECG-ML) model for chronic liver disease risk

links.outcome: Clinician engagement with ECG-ML alerts and its association with diagnostic yield
links.effect: Overall engagement 29.8%; high engagement had higher diagnostic yield for any CLD (22.3% vs 5.0%; OR 3.74, 95% CI 2.44-5.75) and advanced CLD (10.6% vs 2.9%).
links.quote: Among 110 clinicians receiving ≥1 alert (1385 ECG-ML-positive patients), overall engagement was 29.8%.

unlisted_practices: Accounting for clinician engagement when designing and interpreting AI-enabled clinical trials

screen.reason: This is a post-hoc analysis of a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial evaluating how clinician engagement with ECG-ML screening alerts affects diagnostic yield. It observes clinician behavior rather than testing a specific implementation safeguard or organizational deployment practice.
